text.text:
DO NOT STAY HERE
Nothing luxury about this, not a hotel, not a place to bring kids, no one knows what they’re doing, they will lie to you and when you follow up about it everyone says it’s someone else’s job to handle it.
Promised me 2pm check-in over the phone.  Also told me there’s a restaurant in the building I could sit in (was cold outside) until room was ready if I arrived before 2. When I arrived at 2 the room had not been cleaned from previous guest.  I had to flag down a cleaner who had to radio to another cleaner to “rush the cleaning” and it was still not ready until after 3 which is the advertised check-in time. The “restaurant” is a bodega where they serve food.  There are no seats inside.  You can sit outside in an alley where I was with all my luggage as a circle of homeless guys smoked a blunt right next to me.  Room smelled like some kind of wood finish or adhesive.  Had my door pounded down randomly by a maintenance guy answering a call from the previous guest that I was never made aware of and he had to work on the fridge during my stay.  Other than a girl Janelle who was helpful, no one that works here knows anything.  I received wrong information from everyone else I was in contact with on all matters.  I was told they offer a shuttle to the airport.  They never said they charge for this but they do.  They texted me during my stay a coupon for $5 to the “restaurant” downstairs with a link.  Clicked link > restaurant menu > ordered food, no $5.  They’ve been telling me they’ll refund me and it’s weeks later they never did.  I’m told the CEO is reviewing my requests lol.  The CEO… Don’t stay here.

UPDATE: Responding to management’s response.  I have the audio file of the phone call where they promised 2pm checkin BEFORE I booked the room. They didn't say "try" they said I could checkin at 2.  They still haven’t even sent me the $5.  The guy I spoke to told me he’d personally refund me the money for the uber to the hotel admitting the confusion over the shuttle service was on them and I told him not to worry as he told me he has 4 daughters and he told me the “CEO” would likely reimburse me. She did not.

text.text:
Amy Finehouse Lofts and Vacation Rentals were exceptional to rent from. I needed a last-minute local stay for a couple of nights and booked a place in Downtown Dallas. In my rush, I accidentally reserved the wrong unit. At first, it seemed like they might not be able to make the change, but the amazing team at Amy Finehouse went above and beyond. Not only did they help correct the booking, they upgraded me as well.

From reservation to checkout, the customer service and hospitality were truly outstanding. The loft itself was extraordinary: beautiful, comfortable, and exactly what I needed for a stress-free, relaxing stay. Thank you for elevating the bar and providing 10-star service. I highly recommend Amy Finehouse Lofts and Vacation Rentals!

Unfortunately this is not as advertised. Very poor area with an increased amount of homelessness. Trying to enter the building was a task. The building and room had a toxic chemical smell about it. The apartment is far from luxurious.
People standing and shouting in the hallway all night - the room was right by the lift.
The multi story car park is close by but the parking staff are not friendly and keep your car keys in an open, unlocked drawer, free for anyone to help themselves.
We didn’t even last 12hours and we checked out and went elsewhere. When asking for a refund the host stated that no refund was possible and they could have resolved the issues - this is not true as I had messaged them for help to enter the building and I got no response.
This room was not booked under my name, it was booked under my husbands.
Do not stay here!

10/11/2025 - response to owners reply.
As stated, it was booked under my husbands name.
Also, the communication is under my husbands name.
If you carefully read through the multiple reviews from previous guests, we all complain about the same thing - the safety and smell being the main concern.
Your response seems to be automated to a lot of the responses.
It doesn’t matter that it is close an authority’s office, it is still unsafe at night time.
On a better note, we had a fabulous 2 night stay at the Fairmont Dallas and it was walkable distance to some lovely restaurants and we felt much safer as we were able to relax.

text.text:
This place is located a short walk from restaurants and downtown stores. The room design is super interesting, as it's essentially a one, big, converted loft.  Where this hotel really stood out for me was with customer service. The front desk staff was very kind, smiling and helpful but one person really stood out - Scott from the hotel maintenance team.
Being on the 6th floor, I tried my digital key and could not enter the room. Reluctantly, I went back down to the lobby to ask for a physical key to enter my room. As I approached the front desk, I've noticed a huge line of people trying to check-in.  Not wanting to be rude and cut the line, I've noticed Scott in the lobby and I asked if he could help me out with the key.  Scott not only helped me, he did it with a smile on his face!  Then he apologized for the inconvenience and offered a free item from the hotel "pantry" store. I'm so pleased with the service I received at this hotel and with Scott in particular, that next time I'm in Dallas, I will make sure to stay at the same hotel. Thank you Scott and whoever this hotel's manager is.  You led this this team by example and helped set the standards very high.  It is much appreciated!  I'll be sure to come back again.

text.text:
I had a very disappointing stay at this hotel. The walls are extremely thin, and noise from neighboring rooms carries very easily. I barely got any sleep due to loud noise coming from a nearby room. I called the front desk to complain and was told someone would be sent to check, but even after waiting over an hour, nothing changed and the noise continued. I eventually had to handle the situation myself by asking the neighboring room to keep it down, which should never be a guest’s responsibility.

I am a Gold member with Marriott, yet no upgrades or added benefits were offered. When I asked for a bottle of water at check-in, the front desk staff was noticeably rude. I was also told I would be charged $50 for a late checkout, with the manager claiming housekeeping would need to work overtime. This explanation felt unprofessional and came across as an excuse to charge an unnecessary fee rather than provide standard loyalty benefits.

To make matters worse, the hotel was completely out of parking upon arrival. Overall, this stay fell well below expectations and felt like poor business practices aimed at taking advantage of guests rather than providing hospitality. I do not recommend this hotel and would not stay here again.

text.text:
The room was clean and the staff were really helpful and nice. Parking can be confusing, so make sure if you park where it says Platinum you let the staff members know. They will charge you inside the hotel. Do not pay the fee outside and inside-the hotel will give you a discounted rate for 24hrs. I made a mistake and paid double but the staff members gave me a refund without a problem.

The only complaint I have is that there was a weird smell in the room. I could not pin point what it was because the room was in fact clean. I should had let a staff member know but it wasn't that strong. Other than that everything was great. The view was great and the TV worked without problems. I checked in and out without any difficulty.  They do have karaoke nights and a bar at the bottom. This is great if you want ambience.

I initially thought I had lost my wallet after leaving my Uber ride, and I was panicking at the front desk. The staff there urgently assisted me in trying to contact my Uber, but unfortunately, there was no success. Thankfully, I later discovered that I had hidden my wallet in my laptop bag.

I cannot express enough how grateful I am for the front office team who went above and beyond to help me. They assisted me in various ways, from helping me log into my Uber account to calling customer service, and even reaching out to my Uber driver directly. I was relieved to find my wallet safe and secure in my laptop bag.

I want to extend my heartfelt thanks to Asa for his calm and welcoming demeanor, and to Khristian for his prompt support. Both gentlemen were truly among the best staff I have ever encountered during a hotel stay, great restaurant choice btw! Lastly, Emily, the manager, helped in every way possible, and I appreciate all of you more than words can express!

I had such a beautiful and memorable stay at Aloft Austin Downtown. The hotel itself has such a vibrant and modern atmosphere, and being right in the heart of Austin made everything so convenient and enjoyable. From the moment we arrived, everything just felt easy, welcoming, and well taken care of.

What made this stay even more special was that we were celebrating my partner’s anniversary. It turned what was already a great trip into something truly meaningful and unforgettable. Every little moment felt extra special, and the overall experience gave us memories that we’ll always hold onto.

A huge thank you to Ellaine, who genuinely made our stay even more beautiful. Her warmth, kindness, and attention to detail did not go unnoticed. She went above and beyond to make sure everything felt personal and comfortable, and that kind of service really makes a difference. It’s rare to come across someone who creates such a genuine connection with guests.

Overall, it was more than just a hotel stay—it was an experience filled with great energy, meaningful moments, and exceptional service. I would absolutely come back and highly recommend this place to anyone looking for something both fun and memorable in Austin.

text.text:
This hotel was perfect for my last minute stay (I booked around 440 and checked in at 530). The front desk attendants that I interacted with (Christian and another taller, black guy on my Saturday night and an older black guy on Sunday at checkout) were extremely kind, professional and personable.

The hotel lobby is quite large (including a bar-I didn’t get to try, a pool table, sitting areas, grab and go breakfast cafe-didn’t try but it was pricey, gym-nice and clean) The room was clean and roomy with a decent view, the ironing board is pretty short and my toilet had issues flushing at times but it was nothing that would deter me from booking again. Overall, I enjoyed my stay here and it was conveniently located as well, I was able to walk safely and solo to the AT@T Discovery Center. Parking was $17 daily through the hotel and $30 through the actual lot so that was a nice deal. The parking lot was huge but a little ways from the front door. However, they do have carts and up front parking for overnight guests when they don’t fill up. They also have nightly entertainment in the lobby from a solo guitar player… also, the bathroom door is the side mirror and it slides (took me a second to realize that)

text.text:
Hampton Inn & Suites Dallas Downtown is a great place to stay if you want to be in the heart of the city. The hotel is in a historic building, and I loved the wall in the lobby showcasing photos of its original setting, it gives the space character and a sense of history.

The location is a major plus. It’s within walking distance to the AT&T Discovery District, restaurants, museums, JFK landmark, and more. There’s also a Starbucks on the first floor, which is super convenient, and breakfast buffet is served daily on the second floor with a solid variety of options.

The only downside during our stay was that there was no maid service during our two-night visit, which was a bit disappointing. Overall though, the experience, location, and atmosphere easily make this a recommended stay, and I’d definitely consider staying here again.

The only downside during our stay was that there was no maid service during our two-night visit, which was a bit disappointing. Overall though, the experience, location, and atmosphere easily make this a recommended stay, and I’d definitely consider staying here again.

text.text:
Overall, not a bad hotel, but the experience definitely felt more “Carnival Cruise” than luxury hotel.

We arrived before check-in and went up to the rooftop pool around 2:20 PM since rooms weren’t available until 4:00. The rooftop pool itself was honestly overhyped compared to the photos online. The website makes it look much more luxurious than it actually feels in person. There was a DJ and definitely more of a party atmosphere, but we were surprised to hear reserved seating was around $250 (if I heard correctly). Because of that vibe, we ended up going to the second pool instead, which was calmer and honestly more enjoyable. It was nice, just not much of a view.

At 4:00 PM we went to check in, and that was probably the worst part of the experience. The woman working the front desk came across like she absolutely hated her job and acted irritated the entire interaction. We had already prepaid for our room through Expedia, but they still didn’t even have a room ready for us at check-in time.

Once we finally got into the room, we immediately noticed a mold/mildew smell. Later on, we could also smell weed smoke coming through the vent from another room nearby.

The hotel itself has a cool atmosphere and the historic building is unique, but between the misleading marketing photos, check-in experience, and room issues, it just didn’t really feel like the upscale luxury experience we expected.

text.text:
I stayed in Room 709 for my birthday weekend 5/29-30 , and overall I had a really good stay. The hotel is absolutely beautiful. The pictures online look great, but they honestly don’t do it justice. My room was amazing, the view was everything, and one of the main reasons I booked this hotel was because of the soaking tub.

I do want to mention one issue I had with housekeeping. When I arrived, there was hair in the tub. Not gonna lie, that was pretty disgusting. Nobody wants to arrive at their room and find someone else’s hair in the tub, especially when the soaking tub was one of the things I was most looking forward to using during my stay. I reached out to the front desk, and housekeeping came up. Unfortunately, it seemed like they only removed the hair instead of actually cleaning and sanitizing the tub. The tub was still dry and didn’t appear to have been cleaned at all. What really stood out to me was that Morgan from the front desk ended up making sure the tub was properly cleaned while I was away at my event. I appreciated that more than she knows, but honestly, that shouldn’t have fallen on her. Housekeeping should have taken care of it correctly the first time.

Now, I want to give Morgan, Skylar, and Josue their flowers because they were absolutely amazing. Morgan was helpful before I even checked in. She answered my questions through the chat, was always kind, and made me feel taken care of before I ever stepped foot in the hotel. Then, while I was getting ready for an event at the Majestic Theatre, I had a wardrobe malfunction and thought my whole birthday weekend was about to be ruined. Skylar came up to help, Morgan stepped in to help, and they even got Josue involved. The teamwork between the three of them was incredible. They didn’t have to go out of their way for me, but they did, and their kindness and genuine customer service meant a lot.

The housekeeping issue definitely needs attention because something as simple as checking and properly cleaning a tub before a guest arrives can make a huge difference. But I also don’t want this review to go by without recognizing Morgan, Skylar, and Josue. They truly went above and beyond, and they played a big part in making my solo birthday weekend special. Thank you all for your kindness and for making me feel cared for during my stay.

text.text:
Rooms ending in 32 or 33 are notably compact. These particular rooms were not included in the recent hotel renovations. A 28-inch suitcase may be challenging to fully open within these accommodations. However, these rooms do offer desirable corner views, featuring expansive windows that provide a panoramic perspective. All even-numbered rooms from 02-12 and 24-32 have an obstructed view. For guests prioritizing a scenic outlook, alternative room selections are recommended. The bedding consists of softer, "sink-in" style mattresses and exceptionally plush pillows, which may not appeal to all preferences.

The speakeasy venue presented an issue with fruit flies; I personally addressed two, and a third was observed in active flight. Upon inquiry, a staff member acknowledged the persistent nature of the problem, indicating that trap deployment and drain cleaning efforts had been undertaken with limited success. The "sports bar" is primarily a bar area equipped with pool tables, cornhole, and a two-lane bowling alley. It was noticeably understaffed, with a single bartender managing both drink and food orders, and also responsible for delivering food orders to the restaurant and retrieving them due to the absence of a runner or bar back.

Overall, my experience was subpar. Considering the price point, I believe superior accommodations can be found at establishments such as Tru, Hilton Spark, or Embassy Suites.

text.text:
Our stay at Magnolia Hotel Dallas Downtown was very enjoyable overall. First, this is not a knock on the hotel itself, but downtown Dallas traffic is pretty horrible, so be prepared for that when arriving and leaving.

The hotel has a classic old-school feel that gives it a lot of character, and the old Mobil Oil décor throughout the property was a really nice touch. The staff was attentive, friendly, and helpful during our stay, which always makes a difference.

The rooms were comfortable, well-kept, and the bed was especially comfortable for a good night’s sleep. The room rate itself felt fair for the location and quality of the hotel, although the $50 per night parking charge seemed a bit high.

The location worked well for us since there were several very good restaurants nearby, and it provided a quick exit to the tollway the next morning. Overall, it was a comfortable stay with plenty of charm and a convenient downtown location.

text.text:
Mandatory single valet charge of $54. I didn’t have an issue with the charge, I have an issue when I’m walking back from Starbucks at 6am and I see the headlights on with someone inside. It was valet “taking my car to the off site garage a few blocks away.”
I understand there are only like 10 spaces to park next to the building, but when half of them are empty at 6am and the owner isn’t notified to this first. Had it been two seconds later, I would have walked by to see my car gone and thought it was stolen. They literally asked for my number at the little valet booth during check in, seems sensible there’s a reason for this.

This incident made it hard to keep overlooking the outdated room/appliances. If the company can’t be bothered to offer any sort of onsite food,  put an ice machine on more than a single floor of a 21 story building, or contract a single valet fluent in English….  Clearly the guests experience is not high on the priority list.

My dogs bath water was yellow. Stepping in human urine on sidewalks can’t be avoided with the homeless presence on every block. It’s actually insulting that your carpet can’t be changed once in a decade.

Recommend anywhere else if you want to feel even slightly valued as a $157/night guest.

text.text:
My husband and I stayed for a week, so I have a few notes/feedback.

Bottom line, if you need to book a quick stay, this hotel will do in a pinch. It’s in a decent location in relations to Dallas, though you should be warned—there are a lot of homeless nearby, especially on the roads around the hotel and leading into the city, as well as active construction going on right next to the main road leading into the hotel itself, so it’s all a bit hectic.

Pros: Staff was nice. Our room was cleaned promptly every day. Hotel is fun looking, albeit quirky. Room was also quiet, but it faced the parking lot (and not the highway it’s next to).

Cons: Bedding/towels were washed in cheap/scented detergent—for anyone with sensitive skin, you might want to call ahead to see if the hotel can accommodate you, as we never got the chance to ask, and were quite uncomfortable most of our stay. Parking is at $20 a night…which I find quite ridiculous, given how removed the hotel is from the city. If you need a long-term stay like we did, I don’t recommend this hotel, specifically for that reason. Hotels this far out from the main parts of the city should provide free parking for your stay.

Overall, we likely will look to stay elsewhere when we come back to Dallas, but if you’re not picky and are staying for a day or two nearby, this hotel isn’t a horrible option.

We recently stayed at The Lorenzo for a little family staycation and overall it was a really nice experience. The hotel itself is beautiful and the room was clean, stylish, and comfortable. It definitely has a unique personality compared to many other hotels in the area.

The staff we interacted with were nice, but the hospitality felt a little neutral. No issues at all — just not the warm welcome you sometimes expect when arriving at a hotel.

One thing to note is the surrounding area. We walked around a bit and there isn’t a lot within walking distance, so I’d probably rate the neighborhood about a 3 out of 5 in terms of nearby things to do. However, Val’s Cheesecake is within walking distance and that was definitely a highlight for us.

Parking at the hotel is $20 overnight. We ended up choosing street parking instead, which we were a little unsure about at first, but thankfully everything was fine and nothing happened to our vehicle.

Unfortunately the pool was closed during our stay, which we were hoping to enjoy, but aside from that everything else was great.

Overall I would give The Lorenzo a 4.5 out of 5. The property is beautiful and it made for a fun and memorable staycation with my kids.

text.text:
As an interfaith wedding rabbi and officiant, I have officiated weddings in many extraordinary venues over the years. What struck me about The Adolphus was its remarkable sense of history and timeless elegance.

From the moment guests arrived, there was a feeling that they were entering a place that had hosted generations of celebrations. The architecture, grand spaces, and attention to detail created an atmosphere that felt sophisticated and memorable without ever feeling distant or formal.

As someone who spends a great deal of time observing how a venue shapes the experience of a wedding, I appreciated that The Adolphus offered more than beauty. It offered a sense of occasion. The setting elevated the celebration while still allowing the focus to remain where it belonged: on the couple, their families, and the significance of the day.

What I remember most was the balance between grandeur and warmth. The hotel possesses an unmistakable elegance, yet it remained welcoming and comfortable for guests throughout the celebration. That combination is surprisingly rare and helped create an experience that felt both special and personal.

The staff was professional, attentive, and a pleasure to work with. Every interaction reflected a commitment to hospitality and a desire to ensure that the couple and their guests could fully enjoy the occasion.

I would gladly recommend The Adolphus to any couple looking for a wedding venue that combines historic character, exceptional service, and a timeless atmosphere that never goes out of style. It is one of Dallas's true landmarks and a wonderful place to begin a marriage.

I would rate this 6 stars if possible.   Beautiful  hotel that was converted from a bank building.  The esthetic is focused on interesting art pieces. But its the people who take this hotel over the top. Never on all my travels have I met so many wonderful staff who genuinely engaged and seemed to love where they work. I especially want to note Wes and Ray in the restaurant CBD and Ryan in the  spa but by no means were they the only ones who made our stay special.

The rooms were beautiful and comfortable and had a luxe feel to the bedding.  My only dislike was the bathroom (which, BTW, was huge). The new trend in hotels seems to be these glass bathrooms that in my opinion are too open to the rest of the room....I like a little mystery in there and don't need anyone watching my outline brushing my teeth etc. But everything was extremely clean and very nicely done.

The Spa was also a great experience and had all those touches that made it feel decadent but also they did a great job.

CBD was excellent.  Every meal we had there was delicious. Order the chicken...wow. Fantastic! The Italian place was okay but not memorable.

Overall I highly recommend this place. Not sure I will have a reason to go back to Dallas but would go back just to spend time at this hotel again.

text.text:
I live only a few miles away, but I love doing weekend staycations at Mint House Dallas. It is a short, easy ride on the DART train, making it very convenient.

The rooms are clean and well-equipped, but the highlight is definitely the incredible view of the Dallas skyline from the large windows. The Tuft & Needle mattresses are also very comfortable.

Since the hotel is located within Santander Tower, the gym is shared with the residents of Peridot. It is a really well-equipped space, and while it can get busy during peak hours, it is usually completely empty during my 5:00 AM workouts.

If you happen to book a smaller room that doesn't have a dedicated work desk, the building’s business center is fantastic. It has a conference room and private work booths that are perfect for getting some remote work done in a quiet environment.

text.text:
I would not recommend this hotel if you value honesty, clear communication, or reliable service.

We requested a late checkout in advance due to a 7:15 a.m. hospital appointment for our child—information that was clearly communicated and should reasonably warrant basic accommodation or at minimum timely, straightforward confirmation.

Despite there being no indication that the room was booked after us, the request was not confirmed. After significant difficulty reaching a staff member, I was finally assured that our concern was understood and that I would receive an answer first thing in the morning. That did not happen. Nor did the promise to also check our room for a trundle bed being made up due to our late arrival.

With no response provided regarding the late checkout out, and under time pressure, I paid for a late checkout through the website when that option became available about 9 am, simply to ensure we would not be further disrupted during our hospital procedures. Shortly afterward paying for a late checkout, I received a text stating that a complimentary late checkout had already been approved earlier—which was not true. Instead, I could not get anyone to meaningfully engage with me about the ability to secure a late checkout out.

I responded politely, explained that no such confirmation had been given, and asked whether the paid late checkout would then be reimbursed given the conflicting information. After that, I was not given any response - completely ghosted.

The overall experience felt disorganized and, at times, dishonest in its communication. For a hotel, this level of inconsistency and lack of follow-through is unacceptable, especially when traveling for medical reasons

text.text: I booked a one day room though Booking.com for February 7&8. plus I also paid the 7 dollars insurance to make my one day event safe and special. I made a mistake and put February 1&2 which I did not notice until I fully paid. So once I noticed it I quickly called booking.com to fix the situation. I got treated like a criminal instead of a valuable customer. Booking.com and Marriott played a back and forth game of tagg blaming each other just to keep my $104.00. I'm on disability and money doesn't come easy. There's an event I want to attend on the 7th @ Masseys Shots and I haven't been out the house in almost a year. All they have to do is switch the dates. I called Marriott and talked to a front desk member and they told me that the manger said she has better things to do. So she can't and won't come to the phone. How awful and heartbreaking! It's been about 3 days of back and fourth. Why does it take 48 hours to switch dates. I will never use booking.com and book with Marriott. They have turned my vacation into a stressful, overwhelming experience! I suffer from anxiety and depression and I have been inspired tears because of the treatment of both establishments! Even with the insurance they want to keep my money that I had to save up just for a one day event. I haven't been at peace, my heart is racing because I have heart disease. I had to double up on my medication just to calm down. I have to look after me and my 90 year old mother who has dementia and the stress is again overwhelming. We have good days and bad days. But thanks to Marriott and booking.com took my $104 dollars like taking candy away from a baby.

"Fine" summarizes this hotel. The room was clean enough, the staff was friendly, the breakfast was adequate, the coffee was decent, the snack prices were reasonable. But nothing stood out.

I will say the rooms and hallways are dark. Very poor lighting in the rooms, even midday with all the lights on and blackout curtains open, it looks and feels like 9pm in the room. The bathroom fan is a loud, sensory nightmare that roars and rattles. And something (the refrigerator maybe?) was knock-knock-knocking all night. My room door no longer fit properly into the frame, so it took muscle to enter/exit.

If you need a place to stay in Plano, you'll do fine here. But you could do much better too.

The beds were terrible—they felt like sleeping on plastic-wrapped cardboard. Definitely not the comfort you’d expect from a Marriott. No free breakfast, which is laughable given how much they charge per night. The pool was filthy and clearly hasn’t been cleaned in a while.

As if that wasn’t enough, the bathroom was downright gross. The toilet had stains, and there was hair in the shower—clearly no attention to cleanliness or quality control.

This stay was so bad that I am closing my Marriott account permanently. I will never be using Marriott again and I’m actively telling friends, family, and coworkers to avoid them as well. A total embarrassment to the Marriott name.

text.text: Cambria Plano Frisco is an absolute hidden treasure. The hotel is so modern but chic, part lounge, part restaurant, part boutique style but still home away from home very friendly, welcoming hotel. And it smells amazing, especially in the lobby/lounge restaurant area. Rooms very comfortable, very clean, hallways always clean and elevators. I was blown away by the staff from the beautiful ladies at the front desk, Miss Crystal, Miss Crystal going above and beyond and Miss Angela, Miss Angela went above and with a reservation issue through the reservation 800 number, and resolved my issue with complete ease right at the front desk. 🏆Everyone was so accommodating, very friendly. In just the few days I was there it felt like a home away from home not just a hotel. The restaurant staff and the entrees they provide are not just “bar food” the ingredients are super fresh, from breakfast to dinner. As a titanium guest I really appreciated the hospitality. Angel, the bartender made amazing drinks and great conversation. Even the GM, Mr. Alec takes the time to speak with the guests to make sure their stay is going smoothly and if anything is needed to reach out. That means a lot to guests,  at this location you’re more than just a number or dollar sign walking through the door you’re a Choice family member. I will definitely be returning soon! 💯😊💯⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

text.text:
Edit: This building is huge and there are hundreds of guests every day. Katie and staff made a small effort to remedy the situation so I changed my review to two stars but the effort was very minimal comparatively so I left the review below.

Huh, this is so embarrassing though I should probably be embarrassed for the hotel not myself. I came here with my husband on a business trip and I'm afraid to leave the room. Why? ... because I can't get back in! LOL, my husband was told that the door gets jammed at times and you have to jerk it loose or something to that effect. I guess I'm not strong enough to do it. Anyway, I left for the gym and had to call my husband out of his conference to help me get back in. That was  the second time I was locked out. I didn't leave again most of the day just in case.

Later I decided to take a chance and head to the pool. Having my dinner and a drink by the pool, since my husband is out late today, seemed worth it. But guess what.... The pool's closed. I asked the front desk if it was open before I left because I saw the sign earlier and he said yes... well, it's not. I tried to go back to my room and change but guess what else. I'm locked out again! No pool, no dinner, no clothes. I could go downstairs and eat in my swim attire but I have braces on my injured knees so try to use them as little as possible... plus it'd be humiliating. I guess I have no choice but to call and have someone come help me... also embarrassing.

That's not all either. The bathroom door doesn't shut all the way or lock so don't forget to put the privacy sign out if you're planning to shower. Oh and the bathroom door needs wd40. It's almost completely nonfunctional. It fell off the hinges actually. I had to catch the door as it was falling toward me and lift it back onto them.

I havent been outside at all today because I've been so worried about getting locked out of my room. The bathroom door is annoying. The pool really sucks but getting locked out is the worst. It's honestly ruining my entire trip because I'm alone and don't want to ask front desk every time I go to and fro.

displayName.text: The Clara Hotel Plano Tapestry Collection by Hilton

text.text:
Don't you think you should be made aware that the hotel is undergoing renovation prior to making reservations?  Being a Gold Hilton Honors loyal member, you'd think I'd be made aware when booking through the site directly!?  Nope.  To my surprise, walking into the lobby to check in, it's under construction.  I guess I could bear it, because it wasn't on the room floor nor noisy overall, but I think it should be disclosed in advance.

I knew this hotel is a "loft" or "warehouse" type redesign, because I wanted something different and saw the pictures.  I was not expecting our room to NOT have a black-out curtain.  Asking the desk clerk about it: "some rooms do; some rooms don't."  We requested a room change if available, and the clerk never got back to us.  Second request to Jessica the next day yielded a room change (Jessica was great to work with!).

Whoever designed the shower should be fired (not to mention the inconsistent black-out curtain installations).  The water constantly cycled between scorching hot and freezing cold.

Getting coffee in the morning in the restaurant was like an Antarctic expedition.  With temps in the high 30's, the a/c was on and blowing full blast.  Not sure if it was due to the remodel, but we grabbed coffee as fast as possible and headed back to our room to thaw out.

Generally, the staff was courteous and attentive.  It's a shame that they are handicapped by a poorly designed hotel.  Maybe the remodel will fix everything, but how will you know when it's finished?

text.text: Our stay at the NYLO Plano Dallas Hotel was without question the worst hotel stay we have ever had. We booked a block of rooms for our son’s wedding. No one ever told us the hotel was under construction. The property was recently purchased by a new owner and will be called The Clara Hotel. With the construction in the front desk/lobby area, amenities were extremely limited. There were few places we could congregate to visit with our out-of-town guests. They should have had the courtesy to tell us so we could have the option of staying at another hotel. That was the tip of the iceberg. In our room, the shade was broken. The chain the raises and lowers the shade was detached. I immediately informed the front desk of the issue, but it was never repaired during our 3-night stay. Others in our party had issues with moldy comforters, burned out light bulbs that were not replaced, and blow dryers that would produce smoke and a burning odor. I talked with Omor, the hotel manager, about these issues. He told me the construction was mentioned on the hotel website, which was not. He said he would talk with the sales department and get back to me. He did not. The hotel’s lack of customer service is a blight on the Hilton brand. My personal recommendation: If you’re looking for a nice hotel to stay in Plano, avoid this one. There are many other hotels in the immediate area.

text.text:
Had a wonderful stay at an Aloft in Japan last year so decided to try Aloft US.   Unfortunately, it’s just not at the same level.

This is the second Aloft we have tried in the Dallas area.  The lobby area is very similar at birh locations and Japan.  The rooms are also very similar.  The rooms are considered lofts, so they are smaller versus some of the “suites” that have a larger sitting area.  The rooms will have just enough for the bed with a small work table.  It’s all right for a shorter stay.

The biggest issue for us was the “free” breakfast we got as a part of our status.  We were able to order 3 bacon egg and cheese biscuits that had lettuce and tomato.  They are even smaller than it appears in the picture.  For $8, you get a tiny biscuit.  That’s it.  Nothing else.  Let’s just say it left quite a bit to be desired.

When you say “free” breakfast (which is an optional add on or as a perk for the Bonvoy program), I imagined a bit more food than a tiny sandwich.  The bottled drinks were all extra.  Coffee was free.

The location is convenient.  Only a couple minute drive to the Legacy shopping center.

text.text:
Stayed here during a business trip and had a suite with a kitchen and two sleeping areas. The room was clean and the location was convenient, which were definitely positives.
That said, there were several design and maintenance issues that would keep me from staying here again. The separate bedroom doesn't have its own A/C unit, so if you close the door for privacy, very little cool air reaches the room. The shower had extremely low water pressure, the tub diverter didn't fully seal, and the shower head leaked continuously. There were also large holes in the wall where a thermostat or HVAC controller had apparently been removed. The dishwasher is not attached to the wall.

The bedroom door was on spring hinges with no doorstop, making it difficult to keep open without wedging it against the dresser. The bathroom sink drained very slowly as well.
My biggest complaint is the layout. The suite sleeps a lot of people with three beds plus a pullout sofa, yet there is only one bathroom. It would have made much more sense to have two connecting rooms with two bathrooms rather than trying to fit so many sleeping spaces into a single-bathroom setup.
Overall, the room was clean and the location was good, but the combination of maintenance issues and the room design means I would choose a different hotel next time.

I don’t usually leave reviews, but I felt compelled to share my experience before even heading to my flight. Unfortunately, this Staybridge Suites fell well below expectations. text.text:
Great Location, But a Major Safety Concern for Families
This was my 3rd time staying at this hotel because the location is absolutely prime, and I have always loved it here in the past. Unfortunately, my most recent stay last week left me incredibly shaken.
Management assigned us a room with a broken lock on the sliding patio door. I woke up to a parent's worst nightmare: my toddlers (who are almost 3 and under 2 years old) had managed to open the sliding door on their own because the latch wouldn't secure properly.
While I regret not inspecting the door immediately upon check-in, a hotel should never assign a room with a compromised safety latch. High-rise windows and doors need to be fully functional and secure.
I brought this serious safety hazard to the front desk's attention during checkout, but unfortunately, absolutely no one from management has reached out to me since.
On a positive note, we absolutely love the Moxies restaurant located here, and we will definitely be back to eat there again. However, when it comes to staying overnight, safety and guest communication have to come first. I truly hope management thoroughly inspects and repairs these locks immediately so no other family has to experience that kind of scare.
Room number 439 .

Amazing experience!
Had a great stay for a few days while vending at the Changing Life and Destiny convention April 2026…
The room was great, the grounds and building are very clean , well kept and stylishly decorated.
The staff are amazing! Super helpful, genuinely gracious and consistently went above and beyond to accommodate a packed house of vendors and without hesitation helped our booth with all the special requests and needs.

Every staff member i interacted with was great

A few standout individuals on the staff that went above and beyond for myself personally:
Senait (spelling?) from the cafe and food staff was exceptionally courteous and friendly… she worked all day at the cafe and then I saw her again for the banquet in the evening same day .. huge smile the whole time! Paying for the  $12 juice didn’t sting as bad when she was at the register haha

Also Ezekiel at the front desk was awesome, he was bellman, courtesy driver , front desk, and was super friendly and have great vibes

Aurora of the kitchen staff was a joy to interact with as our server at our table during the banquet as well..

Overall a fantastic experience
Perfect venue for a conference or expo
Definitely look forward to staying there again for the next expo

text.text: Have visited here several times now. Very convenient to Ericsson headquarters and many other HQs in the Legacy/Plano area. It's a new hotel so everything is updated and in good shape. The rooms are spacious and laid out very well. Every room has a small kitchen as you walk in with a full fridge, microwave, sink, stove, etc. Given the competitive price for the area having the kitchen is a big plus. The staff are all quite friendly and helpful. Breakfast is complimentary for all guests. I've had better breakfasts, but it's pretty standard so I'm not going to complain. They don't have a bar but they do have a big common area and a pretty well stocked shop/fridge area with beer/wine and frozen/prepared meals. Also, there's a new large convenience store right next door so anything else you need is a two minute walk away. I will continue to stay here when visiting Plano and highly recommend it.

text.text:
This was a terrible hotel experience from start to finish. The staff was neither helpful nor friendly, which immediately set the tone for our stay. Had to wait an “ extended amount of time “ for our room
to be ready.

The AC and heat are motion-sensored, meaning they only work if you’re physically in the room. If you leave for any amount of time, the system shuts off completely. When you return, the room feels stuffy with poor airflow and awful air quality. On top of that, the room had a strong chemical smell, similar to Fabuloso, which made it even more uncomfortable.

When I requested an extra pillow, I was told I had to come down to the front desk to get it myself because they “had no help,” whatever that means. That level of service is unacceptable for a hotel.

Overall, I would not recommend staying here. You’re much better off staying next door or anywhere else.

text.text: The strangest and most suspicious motel stay I’ve ever experienced. First and foremost, we were locked out of our room TWICE, due to a miscommunication between the owner and office staff. The first time the keycard was disabled was the same day we checked in. When we went to check and see what happened in the office, we were told the room wasn’t listed as occupied. It was actually AVAILABLE TO RENT, with all of our belongings inside of the room. They reactivated the keycard and it was settled for that evening. The next day came and we had things planned so once we left out of the room  that morning we did not return until dusk. When we got to the room, once again, we were locked out. The shade on the window was pulled back and the room was completely EMPTY. For the second time, we went to the office. Someone else was tending to the front desk, and she stated that we were never put into the system to begin with. All of our things were bagged up and placed into the maintenance closet to (hopefully) be retrieved.  Things were out of place, granted we did have clothes on the bed but certain belongings that were in the packed bags were out of the original bags they were packed in. Overall, if you can avoid booking for more than one night here, please do so.

I recently had the pleasure of staying at Comfort Inn & Suites, and I must say, the experience was nothing short of outstanding! From the moment I arrived, the staff welcomed me with warm smiles and exceptional hospitality.

One standout team member was Natasha, who went above and beyond to ensure my stay was perfect. Her attention to detail and willingness to assist with any request truly set the tone for an unforgettable experience. Whether it was providing local recommendations or ensuring my room was comfortable, Natasha's service was impeccable.

The hotel itself was clean, well-maintained, and offered all the amenities one could desire for a comfortable stay. The rooms were spacious, and the bedding was incredibly cozy—perfect for a good night's sleep after a long day.

Overall, I would rate my stay at Comfort Inn & Suites five stars without hesitation. If you're looking for a place that offers exceptional service and a welcoming atmosphere, I highly recommend this hotel. Thank you, Natasha, for making my stay so special!

text.text: I stayed here on a Wednesday night unexpectedly due to my semi having a breakdown. (MHC Kenworth customers get a discount!) The rooms are well appointed and clean with basic amenities (mini fridge, microwave, coffee/tea maker, mini safe). As far as I could tell, the electrical outlets in my nightstand lamp weren't working, so I had to use a wall outlet to charge my phone. Not really an inconvenience, but some people might need more. My stay in the middle of the week was quiet and uneventful, which is exactly what I wanted. The staff was the real star of the show, being friendly and helpful but not to the point of intrusion. Shout out to R.L. at the desk and Debbie from the shuttle for top notch guest service! And housekeeping is often the unsung hero of a hotel, and as a guest I rarely get to interact with them, but they're doing a great job of keeping the place clean and presentable. The hotel itself is within walking distance to several restaurants and even a Walmart. Would definitely stay here again, even if I wasn't broken down.

I booked my weekly stay for work here. It's near the data center I'm a manager at.
First off, I booked a handicap accessible room. When I checked in on Monday evening, there were none available. I was placed on the 3rd floor and the elevator was out of order. I had already paid full price for a room I had to drag all my luggage up to. I am a handicap with a prosthetic leg and having to drag luggage up to the 3rd floor is not fun.
Rooms are basic, as good as any other rooms around here. There is construction on the road in front, but close to work.
Knowing the elevator problem probably won't get fixed at my stay here, I will find other hotels that charge a bit cheaper with an elevator that works, because paying over $160 a night with now elevator is ridiculous.

text.text: This was the most disgusting hotel I have ever been to. My family and I stayed in room 216. Our second day there we put the sign on the door requesting our room to be cleaned. When we got back that evening it was not. We had to go downstairs and speak to someone at the lobby the next morning and requested our room to be cleaned. The lady at the front desk was sweet and said she would make sure our room was cleaned. When we got back that evening the room was not cleaned and the shampoo/conditioner was not restocked. In the bathroom there is obvious mold where the shower is and the wallpaper is pealing. All the cleaners did was empty the trash and put some more towels up. Beds were not made and the floor was not vacuumed. The carpet in the rooms are discolored and dirty. I usually don’t walk on hotel floors in my socks but during this trip I did. All the socks I wore turned brown after walking on the carpet. The beds are very uncomfortable and my family and I had trouble sleeping. The WiFi is a joke. You will have to enter a password every time you get back to the hotel and you will randomly disconnect from the WiFi and have to enter the password again. We paid over $600 for a four night stay with the amount we paid I thought the rooms would be clean and comfortable. For anyone looking for a place to stay it is worth paying a higher price to stay elsewhere. I will not be back.

text.text: The hotel is beautiful. They said the hotel is only 25 days old (April 2026). My husband and I stayed here with our 3 children: 4, 2 and 6 months. As lifetime platinum elite members from years of weekly work travel we have grown accustomed to certain amenities. We booked this hotel specifically for the pool. Sadly the pool was heated to 78° per management. My Apple Watch said it was 80°. An outside pool in the heat of the summer might feel nice. But an indoor pool temp of 80° for our toddlers and baby is way too cold. The toddlers were shivering and had blue lips within 30 minutes. We opted not to let the baby kick around because of the temp. The pool area also needs a little love. The tile has no grit and extremely slippery for adults and children. No pool towel rack or dirty towel bin.

text.text:
I have such mixed feelings about this place.

The staff: Everyone was great overall. Larry helped me both over the phone prior to my arrival and when I checked in and he was helpful. Housekeeping found my cup holder in the room and alerted the front desk who promptly called me before I left the hotel. I didn't get the names of the two ladies but I appreciate them very much.

The room: The room was clean but it could use a bit of maintenance. The top hinge for the glass shower door was completely loose and it was difficult to open the shower door without fear of the door falling over so we just kept it open during our stay and tried not to get water out onto the bathroom floor.

There were some towel hooks that were missing or about to fall out.

The incident:

We were microwaving some food and the styrofoam plate started to smoke, which set off the smoke alarm in our room. We tried calling down to the front desk from the room phone but no one answered so we went downstairs and notified them. The front desk did not know how to deactivate the smoke alarm so they sent a custodian to the room to try and turn it off. He couldn't and proceeded to take my pocket knife and cut out the smoke alarm which caused an electrical arc and burnt a hole through my knife. He then taped the exposed cables and just screwed the smoke alarm back in place without re-wiring it and leaving it inoperable.

I hope that this has already been repaired for the next tenant 😬😬😬.

The location: It's located next to the highway with easy access to the on ramp in either direction of travel. It's also close to the main shopping area and restaurants.

text.text:
If you have a service dog, please know your rights under the ADA. This establishment attempted to charge us $150 for our service dog despite that being illegal. She was made to sleep outside and when she barked, the hotel decided to kick us out and refund us. Anyone with a true service dog knows the distress a dog can go through being separated from the person they're trained to protect. I will be filing a complaint with the dept of justice and I hope to God that nobody else has to be preyed on over having a disability nobody ever asks for. If you do take a chance and stay here, please record every interaction you can as Texas is a one party consent state.

Edit to add after seeing similar accounts of gross misconduct: your company policy doesn't override federal law.

text.text:
I recently stayed at this hotel for one night and unfortunately it was one of the more unpleasant hotel experiences I've had in a long time.
The moment I walked into the room, I was hit with a very strong, unpleasant odor — it smelled like a combination of old cigarette smoke, mildew, and something chemically sweet that just wouldn't air out. Even after running the AC on full blast and opening the window (which barely helped), the smell lingered the entire stay and made it hard to relax or breathe comfortably.
The bathroom was even worse. There was visible hair — lots of it — all over the shower floor, on the tiles, and even stuck to the sides of the tub. It clearly hadn't been properly cleaned between guests. To top it off, the faucet in the sink was funky and the water pressure was inconsistent (sometimes a trickle, sometimes normal).
Breakfast was another low point. The buffet area felt chaotic and messy and the whole setup looked unclean. Staff seemed overwhelmed and weren't restocking or cleaning up in a timely manner. What was there was very basic — the usual continental items but poorly presented and not very appetizing.
The only mildly positive thing I can say is that check-in was quick and the front desk staff were polite enough. But that's about it.

text.text:
The Hotel in Forney is quite a distance, though it served the purpose which it was supposed to. It seems to be in an isolated area, where especially at late hours, anything can happen.
When making bookings, it wasn’t indicated that the rooms had adjoining doors, which I’ll have to say was a bit of an inconvenience, because the lodgers next doors were noisy.
As for breakfast, it was a bit monotonous, same energy. It could have been better, but you go with what you have. Half a loaf is better than none.
I just think Hotels since the Covid period have lost their vibe and energy. A lot needs to be done to get things back to making the stay of visitors and lodgers more welcoming, comfortable and satisfying.
All over, it wasn’t too much of an experience.

The night FD staff seems to be teenagers that sit in the lobby on their phones or computers and only come to the desk if prompted. We were told after our 1st night fiasco we would be getting a 20% discount on our stay. Upon checkout, there was no mention of this. When we pressed, we were given about a $20 discount on our SIX night stay. We will happily go back to the Marriott that is 50% more expensive. Well worth it.

Thank you Quality Inn!!!

displayName.text: Spark by Hilton Garland Dallas East

text.text:
I spent four nights here a couple of weeks ago and had a genuinely great stay. My room (Room 124) was spotless and smelled amazing the moment I walked in. I loved the layout—it was right near the exit and the laundry facilities, tucked away at the end with only three other rooms nearby, making it feel very private. Parking was also excellent and never an issue.
​A massive shoutout to Aid at the front desk ZAID! He was an absolute pleasure to talk to every day, incredibly helpful, and truly made my visit memorable.
​There were only two downsides to note. First, the guest room doors slam incredibly hard. One morning I actually had a bad headache and noticed that within a two-hour window, I counted eight doors slamming. Interestingly, the heavy exit doors catch themselves and close silently, so management should look into applying that same mechanism to the room doors to give guests some peace. Second, on my final day, I spotted a baby roach on a towel in the bathroom. Since I was already checking out, it didn’t ruin my stay, but it’s worth noting. The bathroom foundation has a few cracks where they might be getting in, so a little extra pest control and maintenance would easily solve this.

text.text:
Not the worst but not perfect.  I picked this hotel because it had pretty good recent reviews and was on the free trolley line.

The first room we were in had a few ants on the nightstand and it freaked me out. So we were moved, which I appreciated. However, the room we were moved to showed a lot more wear than the previous one (I have attached photos). The room was very humid when we first arrived but it did eventually kind of feel comfortable. I’m not really sure why there is a thermostat on the wall because you have to adjust using the dreaded wall unit and it never stops once it gets to temperature, so it’s constantly on unless you turn it off and it is loud.

The lights are a bit annoying when you first get there because there are no ceiling lights, making it a bit difficult to see while you are hauling all of your luggage in. I was a bit weirded out about the lack of staff really caring about the ants. It did take me a bit to actually feel comfortable in the second room.

No water bottles or anything for my status. Beds are so so. The first set of beds seems newer and more comfortable. Each staff member I encountered was very friendly!

They're still using the Zero soap and lotion instead of moving to the Crabtree and Evelyn. There was also no shower caps, makeup remover, etc.

The trolley service is really great! So helpful for Six Flags and the Rangers game!

Overall, I would stay again, I would just have slightly lower expectations going in than I did this time.

The staff seems disorganized, unprofessional, and unwilling to take responsibility for their mistakes.

Save your money and go somewhere else.

text.text:
Won’t stay again, hotel price tag for motel accommodations.
We paid for a double queen bed room (237$ for a 1 night stay) that was not fully cleaned when we went in there was trash on the counters and questionable fluids on the headboard.
One ply toilet paper, that’s all I need to even say about that.
All three of us staying in the room plus the extra family members in a separate room across the hall all said the beds & pillows were very uncomfortable, we all woke up with sore backs and necks.
On top of sleeping on an uncomfortable bed you can expect to be hot despite the thermostat being as low as it would go at 65 degrees! Room was so hot I didn’t even need the bed covers.
Be aware that you will be paying for any and every extra convenience including 5$ for bottled water.
You have to pay for parking which is included in the room rate but good luck trying to even find a parking spot, the lot is tiny and fills quickly.
They also cut off our room cards access at 9am despite checkout being at 11, me personally I think I should have access to my room for the full duration of our stay. I don’t like leaving for breakfast and coming back to not be able to get into the room.
In summary the hotel is expensive for below average accommodations, I’ve slept at nicer Quality Inn’s for 70$ don’t waste your money here.

text.text:
At this location several times in the past for their cookie tin that costs $15 for 6 cookies with no problems, but this very last time I came in to buy the cookies late at night, they were half done and raw in the center.

I took them back to the hotel, the clerk acted like she didn't believe me.  Made me wait a full hour for a new batch of cookies that never came out.  I left and went back up there the next day to explain to the manager, who wasn't there, but another clerk took over and gave me 7 cookies out of the front desk drawer.
Took them home to find several of the cookies smelled like wet dog had to throw them out.

Don't really like this place.  They nickel and dime you.  You can tell when a business is not doing too well they try to hold on to every nickel and won't accommodate the customer, plus they watch your every move like you are trying to steal something from their snack bar when I was looking for the water jug.

This place also stinks of strong dirty mop water when you first enter.  Drury Hotel on I 30 not far from them is way better, cleaner and accommodates customers, plus Drury has a free breakfast whereas this place charges $16.  Drury also have free soda fountain refills.
I would pick Drury over this place any day.  I only went here for the cookies, and they couldn't even do that right.  My suggestion, not only for this place but many places you visit, is to use your credit card so that you can challenge the charges if they fail to accommodate a bad order.  I paid cash, and will never see the money again they are so hard up over there.  Also, want to point out that when paying cash, this place will not provide a receipt.  I'm wondering about that too.

text.text:
I stayed at the Hilton Garden Inn Arlington for one night with my daughter after a concert. We were really excited about having a fun girls’ night, but the experience ended up being extremely frustrating.

This morning I woke up to an extra charge of almost $400 on my account for a “smoking violation.” We did not smoke, at all. The only thing I used was a curling iron and some hairspray while getting ready.

I called the hotel to try to understand what happened and asked simple questions, like if there was a timestamp, if we were even in the room at that time, or if they checked cameras or had any actual proof. Instead of helping, the person who answered was rude and dismissive. At one point I was on hold for 23 minutes, and when she finally came back she quickly said they’d send a dispute email and then hung up on me before I could even ask anything else.

It honestly felt like they have that “we have enough customers, we don’t care if you’re happy” attitude, which is the worst kind of service. It’s really disappointing to see a Hilton property handle customers this way. They were super friendly when I was there, but after having an issue it was the total opposite. You can tell it’s a leadership issue they are having bc of the poor management or leadership.

Now I’m stuck having to spend my own time disputing a charge that never should’ve been applied without proper investigation.

Also, the breakfast was not worth it at all, about $17 for cereal and what tasted like packaged eggs. Luckily didn’t have to pay due to military. That’s why this Hilton gets one star. Otherwise would be ZeRO.

Overall, I just felt disrespected and brushed off. I would not stay here again.

text.text:
I called weeks before my check in date to change my room from a queen to two doubles. I was told notes would be made and accommodated the day of. I pre paid for my room so I had a zero balance.

Upon checking in the double beds were not given initially and it took a while for the manager to make the changes . I didn’t like being held up at the counter making it look as if I was unprepared and did not try to avoid this hold up. The manager was able to correct it.

Then I was surprised to see a need to pay for a parking pass. On the Hilton site for booking this hotel offered free parking. The manager offered me a courtesy parking pass to make up for the check in issue but still what’s the purpose for the fee there’s plenty of parking and it’s not like they have a courtesy officer  to protect our vehicles.

The manager offered was nice and helpful throughout the stay. The exit experience was offsetting, I messaged the app 2am and 5am asking for a later check out I received no response. I call down at 10am and as soon as I ask the morning was rude and was like “no I can’t give anymore” indicating she had already given out extensions. Mind you I asked for an extension at 2am and 5am.

I go downstairs to start taking my luggage to the car around 10:30 and move my car to the side door to make it easier to bring the rest of my items down and the front staff turned my card off . Mind you when I came she’s sitting at the front counter on her phone .
So I had to walk all the way around to have her turn my card back on. I believe she deliberately turned the card off. It be your own people sometimes.
I get the rest of my items and leave . While putting everything on my phone I get a message on my chat from Hilton saying my extension could be approved for 30 mins which was all I needed initially.

So either the staff at the front heard my voice and just automatically said no just because . Either way it goes I felt like she was discriminating and being disrespectful.

text.text:
First, the rooms were nice, appeared to be very clean and liveable. The attendants were very nice. I do have a problem with several things ... Each time I spoke to someone, I got different responses, and the environment is not suitable for my children.

I stopped by last night because someone in the hotel I was at last night was passing out flyers. The lady called and the guy who answered said they'll accommodate my party. They said that the community was kid friendly. I went there this morning and the guy there was young and Asian descent. He said that the prices on the flyer was wrong and told me a list of places to go. He confirmed that they had 1 and 2 bedroom units available. He refused to allow me to view the unit due to the time that I came, although the guy said it's 24 hrs and I should come in. I came again during "regular business hours". They had a 1 bd room and a studio suite. I was looking for a unit for my 3 boys and I. So the 1 bd room would've been great. The room smelled like WEED! The people in the unit connected to my room smoke. It smelled so bad no amount of plug ins and air freshener would help with that. It smelled so much of weed it was so ridiculous. My sons were complaining. The halls and all throughout the community smelled like weed. A lady was screaming and hollering about her car ran out of gas, and that she needed help. Children was screaming and hollering and crying. It was horrible. The young girl that took my ID called me after 11 PM asking me about my inquiry although I went up there 12 hrs ago. I deliberately told her I have 5 in my party and would need the 1 bd rm only for her to say " I do have a 1 bd room but I cannot accommodate your party" lol. Honey, I came there this morning! She's a young African American descent lady. The older African American descent lady was there giving info with her. They both were really nice but I spoke to a guy that sounded Hispanic, a white lady, an Asian guy, and the African American ladies. That's a bit much. Each person said something different. Obviously, you don't pay attention to your customers. As a licensed Master Cosmetologist, Licensed CNA, & Licensed CMA, I remember who I have dealings with. I have spoken to the community 4 times in 1 day and no one remembers they spoke to me. 😔😂😂😂😂😂🤦🤷 I just moved here. I really should've gotten a place before coming but I'ma thug it out! The Source (my Elohim), nor myself have failed me yet. It's a shame tho. It's hard finding a home or hotel out here lol. Everything is raggedy, run down, super expensive and I'm talking over $5k or higher, strict qualifications. Clean up the neighborhood! The trash cans are running over. There are damaged and broken into cars in the parking lot, folks hanging around outside, children running around without supervision, the elevator don't work, and the one that is working, doesn't work properly. You're over charging for in person, and it's drug infested. We came several times a day & it was all kind of people out smoking, and drinking. Definitely not a place for you or your family if you're not hood, not a drinker or a smoker. If you are, then this place is for you. Each attendant that I spoke to was really respectful and courteous. They just didn't know they spoke to me.

Stay Away from This Place!

My husband and I booked this hotel for one night because we needed to be close to AT&T Stadium. After coming back from a show, we were shocked to find that all of our belongings had been stolen from the room. When we contacted the police, they told us that this wasn’t the first time—it’s apparently a recurring issue at this hotel. According to the officers, the building is constantly targeted, and there have even been reports of people getting killed here. This place is absolutely unsafe. We left immediately and want to strongly warn others: do not stay here. It’s not worth the risk to your safety or your property.

Spent a few days at the hotel with the coffee, breakfast, fitness center and rook solidly satisfying.

The location was great too for someone walking or using a ride share service. There are several convenience stores near by, a Wendy’s hamburger and (not open) an amusement park.

The Wifi was solid and good. I could plug in my own HDMI device to the TV. The rest of the room was clean, fun in style and comfortable.

The hotel lobby is large with multiple areas. I spent time in a few them waiting for people, enjoying coffee or having breakfast.

I think the coffee, tea, hot chocolate and hot water is 24 hours. The hotel store has candy, ramen, juice, water and other items with a microwave and convenient utensils, napkins and plates.

Overall a better choice for a better price compared to an earlier visit. I do enjoy pools but walked instead.

text.text: My honest opinion: I checked in Sunday night after 10pm, 4/19/26, and I'm still here until Friday afternoon, 4/24/26. Front desk staff is nice. My room on the 4th floor was dirty. The blanket smelled that of hot breath. The lady at the front desk was super kind and brought up a clean, fresh smelling blanket. There was hair all over the bathroom and what looked like a booger on the back side of the restroom door. I had housekeeping come the next morning to clean. I always strip the bedding and bundle up soiled towels and place them in a neat pile to help out. Upon doing so, there was SO MUCH HAIR on the mattress protector. Grossed out. I informed front desk and the housekeeping staff, and they cleaned it. The housekeeper lady who came in on Wednesday, 4/22/26, was kind of mean. (Short Hispanic lady with light colored hair.) She came in again today, 4/23/26, and said she needed me to leave the room for 15 minutes, and I told her that I cannot and will not leave because I was working (on my laptop and in the midst of a meeting); I had not had to leave my room before any other day, but I did leave on one day that another housekeeper came just to go get some ice and a snack. Housekeeper apologized for asking me to leave, and I verified with the front desk that I do not have to leave my room while being cleaned. Other than the cleanliness issue and breakfast not being the best tasting, everything else has been great. The room gets super cold (which is what my friend & I like). I normally reside at Hampton Inn Duncanville and Hampton Inn near Las Colinas, occasionally at the Sheraton Downtown... I don't think I will return to this Tru Hilton location.

Room we booked was the Suite with 2 rooms and 2 bath. We loved the space as we brought our mum's and they loved their space too. It was clean, nice and convenient for us.

text.text:
Staff accidentally gave or room away due to airport issues, after driving 11hrs to find this out was a let down. We called and confirmed and traveling with multiple kids this wasn't ideal. They did their best to make it up. Now that that's out of the way.

The rooms were definitely dated. The stove in one room was broken and fixed with duct tape. Carpet peeling up, and the pull out was definitely not checked or clean in awhile...

That aside, and doesn't surprise me for Texas, that property was really trashy. Overflowing trash can outside building b entrance. It was overflowing when we got there at midnight and was still overflowing when we left the next morning at 9a. Trash on the ground, spread out everywhere. On a handicap ramp this was not a good look.

Trash throughout the grassy areas where I was walking my dogs.

For the Marriott brand this location missed the mark.

Staff was friendly and kids enjoyed breakfast. Unless there is desperation I won't plan to stay here again

text.text: The front desk person was magnificent.  That is where magnificent stops. There was a purse that had been gone through at the parking lot.  Showers are ice cold at 7am. The chair is torn up on the back. I could get one at a garage sale in better condition.  The tiles looked like they got a friend of a friend to do it instead of a professional.  The fridge sounded like a freight train and it was marked up. This was not Marriott quality.  They asked everyone if they wanted the 1st floor. I don't want to know what the upper floors are like. I only took a few pictures like the wall joints coming loose but there is plenty more to see if you want to find out for yourself.

text.text: Stayed for an event in town.  Room  and furniture is out dated.  Bed was comfortable.  Breakfast was ok.  Free.  Front desk was accommodating to my needs. If you have pets this is the place for you. There's better options for hotels if you have no kids or pets around .

text.text:
Excellent place to stay, the room was quite cozy.
The facilities were clean and the staff very friendly.
The breakfast was good and the portions generous.
The juice machine wasn't working, and Valeria, the very kind girl who worked in the dining area, came over and offered to give me some juice.
